posts.title: Switching To More Efficient Keyboard Layouts
posts.description: For some years now, Google's default keyboard has not been very good at swipe input. It's way too often that I have to fix words that it guesses. Coupling that with concerns for privacy, it led me to search for an alternative. After looking at the alternatives, I installed FUTO keyboard. When going through the settings, I noticed it had a KASROZ layout that has been optimized for swiping that's ideal for a one handed layout. This gets into another gripe of mine... Phones Should Be Made For One Handed Use, but I'll discuss that another time. I started using it, and it hurt my brain quite badly at first, but after just a single day I'm already starting to pick up on it, and I can tell it's better than swiping on QWERTY. I imagine in about a month I'll be fluent with it and the pain will finally be over. This got me thinking, why use QWERTY for my physical keyboard? posts.title: Finding My Writing Voice In The AI Age
posts.description: AI is great for exploring thoughts, and I've used it heavily to help me write some of the notes in my digital garden. One thing I've found however is that it results in me losing my "voice": my distinct writing style. While my writing style is remarkably similar to that of a lot of AI models (probably because I'm really analytical and formulaic?), it's not identical. In order to keep my writing style my own, I think I need to write enough 100% original content unaided, and never dump raw AI output into my notes. When using an AI to help me write some of my notes, I can have it learn from my tone from these notes to get me closer. It's better to use AI to help clarify the ideas, or to criticize my writing to come up with points for improvement, and then manually write my own changes. The danger of losing my voice is real, and I imagine something all of us are dealing with right now, and we need to fight back against the temptation of using the AI chatbots to do our thinking for us. posts.title: The Hollyhock Weevil and Creation
posts.description: On 2026-09-14, a coworker showed me a bag of hollyhock seeds he had picked on one of his walks. I looked closely and saw little tiny bugs moving around. I took out my phone and took a picture zoomed in to get a better look: These things were tiny, no longer than 1/8th of an inch. A prompt to an AI model quickly told me what they were: Rhopalapion longirostre , commonly known as the hollyhock weevil. I read up on them on various sites: https://www.gbif.org/taxon/SL735 https://bugswithmike.com/guide/arthropoda/hexapoda/insecta/coleoptera/polyphaga/curculionoidea/brentidae/apioninae/rhopalapion/longirostre https://gardenerspath.com/plants/flowers/hollyhock-weevils/ I was amazed to find out that this bug is 100% reliant on plants in the mallow family, especially hollyhocks. This kind of struck me: God's creation is amazingly intricate. The fact that there's such a bug just astounded me.
